headline: Orders and margins surge, GE Vernova raises guidance
summary_short: GE Vernova's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 22% year-over-year to $11,104 million on strong Power and Electrification equipment growth, with orders up 88% organically to $24.2 billion; adjusted EBITDA rose 62% to $1,250 million and the company raised its FY2026 revenue and free cash flow guidance.
summary_long: Revenue grew 22% y/y (12% organically) to $11,104M, led by Gas Power equipment and Electrification grid demand, partially offset by softer Onshore Wind equipment. Segment EBITDA margins expanded meaningfully: Power +240bps to 18.8%, Electrification +390bps to 18.4%, while Wind margin fell to -13.6% on higher Offshore Wind project costs. Net income was $668M and diluted EPS $2.47 (+33% y/y); adjusted EBITDA rose 62% to $1,250M. Free cash flow of $5,107M (+$4.9B y/y) reflected working-capital benefits, funding $2.3B of buybacks and a $0.50/share dividend; cash ended at $13.1B. Management raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $45.5-$46.5B and free cash flow guidance to $11.5-$12.5B.
confidence_notes: FORCE-REGENERATED — this summary was regenerated on explicit request, overwriting/writing fresh at data/summaries/GEV_US_FY2026_Q2.json (no prior summary file existed for this period, so this is a fresh write rather than a true overwrite). Net income KPI ($668M, from the shard's Yahoo-sourced net_income_usd_m) differs from the release's own GAAP net income of $649M — both provenance families report net income but the shard figure derives from Yahoo fundamentals-timeseries rather than the primary filing table; the release figure is authoritative for the driver narrative above. The Adjusted EBITDA KPI ($1,250M) is the company's own non-GAAP measure (excludes restructuring, separation costs, pension items, and one-time gains such as the Prolec GE remeasurement); it differs from the shard's unadjusted ebitda_usd_m KPI (~$1,072M, ≈ operating income + D&A) — a legitimate GAAP-vs-non-GAAP basis difference, not a data error. Q1 FY2026 net income and diluted EPS comparatives (prior_qq: $4,745M / $17.44) were inflated by a one-time ~$3,992M pretax gain on the Prolec GE remeasurement recorded that quarter — not a Q2-vs-Q1 operating trend. The Orders KPI (+88%) is the company's own organic growth rate (ex-FX/ex-M&A); a consolidated GAAP orders y/y figure was not broken out in the release (only segment-level GAAP orders were given).

drivers.explanation: Growth was led by equipment growth at Electrification and Power, along with higher services across segments, partially offset by lower Onshore Wind equipment deliveries.

Driven by robust Gas Power equipment demand (52 heavy-duty units) and Electrification grid equipment strength, including data center orders over $5B YTD; partially offset by lower Onshore Wind orders.
Margin expanded from higher volume, price, and productivity; Electrification segment margin rose 390bps and Power rose 240bps, partially offset by wider Wind segment losses.
Increase of $4.9B was primarily due to higher positive working-capital benefits and stronger Adjusted EBITDA versus the prior-year quarter.
Management framed the quarter as strong execution on backlog and orders growth, margin expansion, and cash generation, prompting raised FY2026 revenue, free cash flow, and segment guidance.
